cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the questions are the work right now.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're moving toward and ask someone a real question about it today — something you don't already know the answer to.
cells.core:
You're learning the shape of the thing before you move on it. That's not hesitation — it's how you keep from walking into walls. You ask, you listen, you turn things over, and the direction gets clearer as you go. Nothing flashy about it, but it works, and it's holding.

The balance is worth keeping, and it costs something. Curiosity can become its own destination if you let it — one more question, one more stone turned, and the moving doesn't start. The structure that serves you is the one that lets you ask and then act on what you find. Say what you learned and what you're doing about it, out loud, to one person who'll hold you to it.
cells.sheetLine: You learn the road by walking it, and it's working.
cells.verb: learning the shape of the thing before you move on it
cells.place: the road that only becomes a road by walking it

cells.tense: You are already at the end of a road that hasn't been built yet.
cells.ask: Before you move on the next thing, write down three questions you haven't asked — and sit with them for an hour without answering.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward an end that isn't here yet. Every question has become a way to get somewhere faster, and the getting has eaten the learning. You're asking to close the gap rather than to see it, and the gap keeps moving because you won't let it stay open.

The curiosity is real. It's just running ahead of the thing it's supposed to be discovering. When you're back in step, you can sit with not knowing and still move; what you find lands on its own, without you forcing it. Right now you're braced against a future you can't write into. Ask your questions, then stop. Let one answer come to you instead of hunting it down.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that's already behind you, and your hand's still on the knob.
cells.ask: Name one thing you used to be curious about and tell someone about it — not what you learned, just what you noticed.
cells.core:
Reaching toward the next thing because you want to see it — that's how this goes when it's healthy. You ask because the answer is interesting, not because it gets you somewhere, and the direction holds itself up without much pushing from you.

What's happening now is quieter. The questions stopped and you didn't notice when. You move toward goals without looking at them too closely, and the road is narrower than it was. What's gone isn't a destination — it's the pull toward looking. The curiosity hasn't left. It's just uncharged, and pushing it directly won't work; effort into a starved place makes it worse. Let yourself imagine again, loosely, without a destination. Wonder about something small and let it be pointless. Direction comes back on its own once the dreaming has somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking, and you didn't see it happen.
cells.verb: learning the shape of the thing before you move on it
cells.place: the road that only becomes a road by walking it

cells.tense: You are already learning the road, and you're calling it just getting there.
cells.ask: Catch one thing you figured out this week and say out loud that you're the one who figured it out.
cells.core:
When this side of you is clear, you're taking things in — noticing, adjusting, finding the shape before you commit — and you'd tell anyone that the figuring out was yours. The learning and the saying-so run together, and the direction stays steady because you're walking it on purpose.

Right now the learning runs but the claim doesn't. You describe it as just moving, just handling it, just doing what's next. The curiosity is there the whole time; you've stopped signing your name to it. Fairness to yourself is the work here: you give credit out freely, but the one who's actually doing the work doesn't get counted. When you look at what you've learned and say it's yours, the direction gets steadier. Start with one thing. Say you found it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already learning it — the credit just isn't yours yet.
cells.verb: learning the shape of the thing before you move on it
cells.place: the road that only becomes a road by walking it

attempts.check: The record supports: the card's behavior (fresh curiosity, listening, questioning), the seat (directed momentum toward goals), and the four statuses with their medicines. It does not support any claim that the person's history caused this, nor what they feel underneath, nor praise for a method I invent for them. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line that tells them what they are 'really' doing underneath — those are cut.
